title: Every quasi-compact open of an affine scheme with one-dimensional Noetherian local rings is affine

standard_prerequisites.name: Higher direct images along the inclusion of a quasi-compact open in the one-dimensional affine case vanish
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the vanishing of R^p j_*F which makes the Leray sequence collapse.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves on affine schemes and the Leray spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero (tag 01XB); Cohomology, Lemma cohomology-lemma-apply-Leray (tag 01E3)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the vanishing on X and the spectral sequence transferring it to U.

core_obligations: Let j : U -> X be the inclusion and let F be a quasi-coherent O_U-module; use the affine-curve lemma to see that the higher direct images R^p j_*F vanish (proof lines 7779-7782).
Observe that j_*F is quasi-coherent on X and hence has vanishing higher cohomology because X is affine (proof lines 7782-7787).
Apply the Leray spectral sequence to conclude H^p(U, F) = 0 for all p > 0, and deduce that U is affine from the vanishing criterion for quasi-compact opens (proof lines 7788-7793).
proof_roadmap: Kill the higher direct images along the open immersion.
Use affineness of X for the pushed-forward module.
Run Leray to get vanishing on U.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a quasi-compact open U of an affine scheme whose local rings are Noetherian of dimension at most one is itself affine. The proof lets j : U -> X be the inclusion, takes a quasi-coherent F on U, kills the higher direct images R^p j_*F using the affine-curve lemma, notes that j_*F is quasi-coherent on the affine X and hence has vanishing higher cohomology, and concludes via the Leray spectral sequence that H^p(U, F) = 0 for p > 0, which characterizes affineness for quasi-compact opens (proof lines 7779-7793). H2: the merging of three cited cohomological tools into the vanishing criterion is the substance and is not a one-line citation.
